title: Quantization quality regression cases (collected examples + targeted eval ideas)
content:
Context
- We keep seeing “small” quantization changes (e.g., FP16 -> INT8, INT8 -> INT4, FP8 activation paths) cause non-obvious product regressions.
- This doc collects real-ish symptom patterns observed in internal experiments + a few customer escalations.
- Goal: turn these into targeted eval cases/sentinels so guardrails gating can reliably catch them (esp. formatting/tool-calling/structured outputs).

How to read
- Each case: (1) symptom; (2) likely quantization driver; (3) affected model families (observed / suspected); (4) quick reproduction prompt idea; (5) proposed eval(s) we should add.
- NOTE: not all cases are “quantization-only” — some are quantization + decoding or batching/caching interactions. Still useful because Optimize proposals often bundle changes.

Non-goals
- Not a comprehensive benchmark.
- Not deciding the global thresholds here (see Applied ML tuning scratchpad / threshold ADR).


Case 01 — Structured output JSON becomes invalid (trailing commas / unescaped quotes)
Symptom
- Tool-calling or structured output responses stop being parseable JSON.
- Common failures: trailing commas, missing closing braces, unescaped newlines, double-quoted keys turning into single quotes.
Likely driver
- Lower-precision logits magnify “near tie” token choices for punctuation/quotes.
- Observed more when quant profile changes also alter kernel selection / softmax stability.
Affected models (observed)
- Llama-3.x (8B/70B) under INT4 weight-only profiles
- Mixtral variants under aggressive INT4 + KV cache compression
- Qwen2.x (esp. tool templates with lots of quotes/braces)
Repro prompt idea
- “Return STRICT JSON only. No prose.” with nested objects + arrays + special characters.
- Include a field with a string that itself contains quotes and newlines.
Proposed eval additions
- Hard parser check: 100% of samples must parse as JSON (no retries).
- Schema validation: required keys + type checking.
- Add a “JSON edge” mini-suite: 20–40 prompts covering nested structures + escaped strings.


Case 02 — Function/tool selection drift (wrong tool chosen)
Symptom
- Model selects the wrong tool among 2–5 options; correct tool choice drops significantly.
- User sees “it called the wrong API” even though natural language looks fine.
Likely driver
- Small distribution shifts around tool name tokens and argument keys.
- Quantization can change relative ranking between near-equivalent tool calls.
Affected models (observed)
- Qwen2.x Instruct
- Llama-3.x Instruct when tool list is long
Repro prompt idea
- Provide 3 tools with overlapping descriptions (“search_docs”, “search_tickets”, “search_users”) and require correct selection based on subtle hints.
Proposed eval additions
- Tool-choice accuracy metric (exact match on tool name) separate from argument JSON validity.
- “Confusable tools” suite: prompt templates with minimal lexical cues.


Case 03 — Formatting drift in constrained outputs (bullet lists / numbered steps / markdown tables)
Symptom
- Output format breaks product rendering assumptions (missing numbering, inconsistent bullet indentation, table column count mismatch).
- In some customers: breaks downstream extraction or UI display.
Likely driver
- Quantization increases entropy on whitespace/punctuation tokens; also changes stop-token behavior indirectly.
Affected models (observed)
- Mistral / Mixtral Instruct (INT4)
- Gemma family under certain AWQ/GPTQ variants
Repro prompt idea
- “Produce a markdown table with EXACTLY 4 columns: A|B|C|D. 10 rows.”
- “Return exactly 7 numbered steps, no extra text.”
Proposed eval additions
- Deterministic format validator: count rows/cols; regex checks for numbering continuity.
- Add “format strictness” prompts to sentinel suite.


Case 04 — Latent reasoning degradation (passes surface checks, fails multi-step)
Symptom
- Short, easy questions look okay, but multi-step reasoning accuracy drops (math word problems, chain-of-thought hidden, planning).
- User reports “it’s dumber” with no single obvious error mode.
Likely driver
- INT4 weight-only sometimes disproportionately impacts attention/MLP layers needed for longer reasoning trajectories.
- More pronounced at longer outputs (>256 tokens) and with higher temperature.
Affected models (observed)
- Llama-3 70B class under aggressive INT4
- Some Phi-class small models under INT8 (less headroom)
Repro prompt idea
- GSM8K-style word problems; multi-constraint scheduling (“3 meetings, time zones, availability”) requiring consistent intermediate state.
Proposed eval additions
- Reasoning suite gating for quant transitions above a risk threshold (esp. INT8->INT4).
- Score via exact answer + consistency checks (units, date formats).
- Minimum sample size: needs enough items to beat noise; consider 100+ for this suite.


Case 05 — Refusal / safety boundary shift (either over-refusal or under-refusal)
Symptom
- Quant profile change changes safety behavior:
  - Over-refusal: harmless requests refused.
  - Under-refusal: borderline content compliance increases.
Likely driver
- Small logit shifts near policy boundary phrases; quantization noise can flip refusal templates.
Affected models (suspected + some observed)
- Llama-3.x Instruct
- Qwen2.x Instruct
Repro prompt idea
- “Benign-but-sensitive” prompts: medical advice disclaimers, mild self-harm mention in fictional context, etc.
Proposed eval additions
- Lightweight refusal classifier + “policy boundary” prompt set.
- Track both false positives and false negatives.
NOTE
- Coordinate with Security/Compliance on what can be stored as eval artifacts.


Case 06 — Increased hallucination on retrieval-grounded prompts
Symptom
- In RAG-style prompts with provided context, model cites facts not in context more often.
- Especially when asked to quote exact phrases.
Likely driver
- Quantization changes attention to context vs prior; also changes copy fidelity for exact spans.
Affected models (observed)
- Mixtral variants under certain INT4 kernels
- Llama-3.x under FP8 activation path (experimental)
Repro prompt idea
- Provide short context with distractor facts; ask for exact quote + citation line numbers.
Proposed eval additions
- “Context faithfulness” checks: answer must be substring of context for quote tasks.
- Citation correctness metric (if we require citations).


Case 07 — Multilingual / code-switching quality drops disproportionately
Symptom
- English looks fine; Spanish/Japanese/Arabic drops (grammar, politeness, incorrect scripts), or code-switching becomes erratic.
Likely driver
- Token distribution differences; some languages rely more on rarer tokens and longer token sequences.
Affected models (observed)
- Llama-3 8B/70B under INT4
- Gemma under some quant profiles
Repro prompt idea
- “Respond in Japanese using polite form, include 3 bullet points and a closing sentence.”
- Code-switch: “Explain X in Spanish but keep key technical terms in English.”
Proposed eval additions
- Add a multilingual slice to sentinel suite (small but representative).
- Score via LLM-as-judge rubric, but also add simple script/charset checks.


Case 08 — Logprob/temperature sensitivity spike (behavior changes more with small decoding parameter tweaks)
Symptom
- With quantization profile B, small changes in temperature/top_p cause large semantic drift vs baseline.
- Customers interpret as “less stable” across retries.
Likely driver
- Quantization alters calibration; distribution becomes flatter/peaky in different regions.
Affected models (observed)
- Mistral family under INT4
- Smaller models under INT8
Repro prompt idea
- Run same prompt at temperature 0.2 vs 0.3; measure semantic similarity / answer consistency.
Proposed eval additions
- Stability metric: agreement across N samples under fixed seed range.
- For gating: at least detect large increase in variance vs baseline.


Case 09 — Stop token / EOS behavior changes (truncation or run-on)
Symptom
- Outputs truncate early (missing closing brace) OR run on past expected stop sequences.
- More frequent “never stops” in streaming until max_tokens.
Likely driver
- EOS token probability shifts; stop sequence match becomes less likely with punctuation drift.
Affected models (observed)
- Llama-3.x, Qwen2.x (tool templates)
Repro prompt idea
- Force a clear delimiter stop: “END_JSON” or XML close tags; verify it appears.
Proposed eval additions
- Stop-sequence hit-rate check.
- Validate presence of required terminators for structured formats.


Case 10 — Numeric formatting drift (commas/decimals, scientific notation) impacting downstream parsers
Symptom
- “1,000.00” becomes “1000,00” or “1 000,00” depending on locale; or produces scientific notation unexpectedly.
- Breaks finance/analytics ingestion.
Likely driver
- Token choice instability for punctuation and separators.
Affected models (observed)
- Qwen2.x
- Mistral Instruct
Repro prompt idea
- “Return numbers formatted as en-US with 2 decimals.” Provide multiple values.
Proposed eval additions
- Regex-based numeric formatting checks.
- Add locale-sensitive prompts to coverage plan.


Case 11 — “Echo” / repetition loops increase
Symptom
- Repeats phrases or lines, especially in longer outputs.
- More “As an AI language model…” templates repeating.
Likely driver
- Quantization affects repetition penalty dynamics; near-duplicate token scores become harder to separate.
Affected models (observed)
- Mixtral variants under INT4
- Some smaller instruction models under INT8
Repro prompt idea
- Ask for a 400–800 token explanation with section headings; detect repeated lines.
Proposed eval additions
- Repetition rate metrics (distinct n-grams / self-BLEU).
- Clamp: fail gating if repetition exceeds baseline by X.


Case 12 — Hidden interaction with caching/batching: ordering / role prefix corruption
Symptom
- In chat, role prefixes (“assistant:”) leak into content; sometimes “system” tokens appear.
- Seen when quantization change coincides with new KV cache / batching policy.
Likely driver
- Not purely quantization: altered kernel path + cache reuse patterns.
- But quantization makes the format brittle, exposing upstream prompt-template issues.
Affected models
- Llama-3 chat templates (observed)
Repro prompt idea
- Multi-turn chat with strict “DO NOT include role labels” instruction.
Proposed eval additions
- Chat hygiene checks: role label leakage detection.
- Multi-turn sentinel prompts with tool-calling + follow-up summarization.


Notes on model families / profiles (rough)
- “Highest risk” transitions (based on our historical flake/regression rate):
  - FP16/BF16 -> INT4 (weight-only)
  - INT8 -> INT4
  - Any profile that changes activation precision (FP8-ish paths) for long-context workloads
- “Lower risk” (still not safe):
  - BF16 -> INT8 (weight-only) on some mid-size models


Proposed minimal targeted sentinel suite for quantization gating (v0 idea)
- Structured JSON validity: 25 prompts
- Tool selection (confusable tools): 30 prompts
- Format strictness (tables/numbered lists): 20 prompts
- Context faithfulness (quote/cite): 25 prompts
- Multilingual slice: 15 prompts (5 es, 5 ja, 5 ar)
- Reasoning slice: 50 prompts (mix math + planning)
Total: ~165 prompts (too big for “fast” gating; might need tiered suites)

Tiering suggestion (runtime POV)
- Fast suite (<=5–8 min target): JSON validity + tool selection + format strictness (high customer impact, fast to score)
- Standard suite (<=20–30 min): add context faithfulness + some multilingual
- Full suite (offline/backfill): add reasoning + stability metrics + repetition checks


Open questions / TODOs
- Should JSON validity be a hard block (100%) for tool-calling routes? I think yes.
- How do we keep eval artifacts PII-safe for enterprise prompt sets? Need redaction + allow customer-managed artifacts.
- Need to map these cases to ENG-3921 “unsafe transitions” list and decide mandatory suites per transition.
- For customers w/ strict SLOs: do we allow async apply (apply pending) vs blocking apply? Product decision.


Recent references / why this exists
- SUP-18422: customer reported quality regression after Optimize applied a more aggressive quant profile (symptoms: JSON/tool args malformed + more hallucination).
- Slack quantization thread: consensus that we need mandatory suite list for quant changes + per-model exclusions.

Changelog
- 2025-01-09: initial dump from runtime + a few Applied ML notes
- 2025-01-28: added tool-selection drift + stop token behavior
- 2025-02-14: added tiering suggestion + multilingual slice + caching/batching interaction note
